summary:
John chapter 1 introduces the profound mystery of the Incarnation, establishing Jesus Christ as the eternal Word (*Logos*) who existed before creation, co-existed with God, and is fully God. As the source of life and light, the Word became flesh to dwell among humanity, revealing the Father’s glory, grace, and truth. John the Baptist serves as the primary witness to this arrival, humbly pointing away from himself to identify Jesus as the preexistent One and the sacrificial "Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world." 

The chapter transitions from high theology to personal relationship as Jesus begins calling His first disciples. Through the testimonies of Andrew, Philip, and Nathanael, Jesus is recognized as the Messiah, the Son of God, and the King of Israel. By inviting them to "come and see," and promising that they will see heaven opened upon the Son of Man, Jesus positions Himself as the ultimate bridge between God and humanity, setting the foundation for the journey of faith detailed in the rest of the Gospel.
